business_rules: Email addresses are evaluated case-insensitively for account lookup.
A user can belong to multiple organizations using a single account.
Unverified accounts remain inactive until email verification is completed.
Password reset mechanisms must not expose whether an email address exists in the system.
Password reset links and temporary authentication tokens must have a limited lifetime.
Changing a password or executing sensitive security actions must invalidate existing active sessions.
Raw passwords and password-reset secrets must never be stored in plaintext.
Account deactivation preserves historical activity logs and system references.

functions.signature: register_user(email: str, password: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Registers a new user account and sends a verification email.

functions.signature: verify_email(token: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Validates the email verification token and activates the account.

functions.signature: request_password_reset(email: str) -> None
functions.purpose: Generates a password reset token if the account exists without revealing account existence.

functions.signature: reset_password(token: str, new_password: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Resets the user password and invalidates all existing user sessions.

functions.signature: update_profile(user_id: str, display_name: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Updates user profile details such as display name.

functions.signature: deactivate_account(user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Deactivates a user account while preserving historical records.

business_rules: The initial user creating an organization becomes its owner.
Organizations are strictly isolated; authorization boundaries apply at the tenant level.
Organization display names need not be globally unique, but short URL identifiers must be unique.
Invitations are sent to email addresses; accepting an invitation joins an existing account or triggers registration.
Invitations expire after a set duration and can be explicitly revoked by an administrator.
Organization access roles are categorized into owner, administrator, and member.
Ownership transfer changes organizational responsibility, requires designation of a valid recipient, and logs the action.
Removing a member immediately revokes access but does not erase historical activities or work assignments.

functions.signature: create_organization(name: str, owner_id: str, short_identifier: str | None = None) -> dict
functions.purpose: Creates a new organization workspace and sets the creator as initial owner.

functions.signature: invite_member(org_id: str, email: str, inviter_id: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Sends an invitation email to join an organization.

functions.signature: accept_invitation(invitation_token: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Processes an invitation token to add a user to an organization.

functions.signature: revoke_invitation(org_id: str, invitation_id: str, admin_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Revokes an outstanding invitation before it is accepted.

functions.signature: transfer_ownership(org_id: str, current_owner_id: str, new_owner_id: str, new_role_for_previous_owner: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Transfers organization ownership to another active member.

functions.signature: remove_member(org_id: str, member_id: str, admin_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Removes a member from an organization and revokes workspace access.

functions.signature: update_organization_settings(org_id: str, name: str | None = None, timezone: str | None = None) -> dict
functions.purpose: Updates organization settings such as display name and default timezone.

business_rules: A project belongs to a single organization and serves as a primary grouping mechanism for work.
Project creators normally become initial project owners.
Project access is distinct from organization membership; only organization members can join project membership.
Archiving a project removes it from active working views while preserving data for historical inspection.
Completing a project indicates work reached its intended conclusion and is distinct from archiving.
Project names do not need to be globally unique within an organization.
Project deletion is destructive and must cascade or safely handle dependent work items, comments, attachments, and logs.
A project must retain an active responsible owner.

functions.signature: create_project(org_id: str, name: str, creator_id: str, description: str | None = None, due_date: str | None = None) -> dict
functions.purpose: Creates a new project within an organization.

functions.signature: add_project_member(project_id: str, user_id: str, requester_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Adds an existing organization member to a project.

functions.signature: remove_project_member(project_id: str, user_id: str, requester_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Removes a user from a project while preserving assigned work items.

functions.signature: archive_project(project_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Archives a project to remove it from primary active views.

functions.signature: complete_project(project_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Marks a project as completed.

functions.signature: delete_project(project_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Destructively removes a project and cleans up dependent resources.

business_rules: A work item belongs to exactly one project and requires a title and a status.
Initial statuses include not completed, in progress, and completed.
Completed work items can be moved back to active states.
Work item assignees must be valid project members.
Due dates represent calendar days rather than exact timezone-dependent instants.
Priority levels are represented using a small ordered range rather than arbitrary numeric codes.
Removing an assignee or due date leaves the field blank without destroying history.
Work item edits generate activity feed entries and must handle concurrency safely.

functions.signature: create_work_item(project_id: str, title: str, creator_id: str, description: str | None = None, priority: int | None = None, assignee_id: str | None = None, due_date: str | None = None) -> dict
functions.purpose: Creates a work item in a specified project.

functions.signature: update_work_item(work_item_id: str, user_id: str, title: str | None = None, description: str | None = None, status: str | None = None, priority: int | None = None, assignee_id: str | None = None, due_date: str | None = None) -> dict
functions.purpose: Updates attributes of an existing work item.

functions.signature: remove_due_date(work_item_id: str, user_id: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Clears the optional due date from a work item.

functions.signature: reorder_work_items(project_id: str, work_item_ids: list[str]) -> bool
functions.purpose: Reorders work items within project views according to user preference.

business_rules: Comments belong directly to work items; threaded discussion is excluded in the initial release.
A comment contains an author, body, creation timestamp, and optional edited status.
Users can edit their own comments.
Organization administrators can moderate comments in exceptional circumstances.
Deleting a comment replaces content with a removal indicator without wiping activity records.
Comment text is treated as untrusted input and must be safely escaped before rendering.

functions.signature: add_comment(work_item_id: str, author_id: str, body: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Adds a contextual discussion comment to a work item.

functions.signature: edit_comment(comment_id: str, user_id: str, new_body: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Edits the body of an existing comment and sets the edited state.

functions.signature: delete_comment(comment_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Soft deletes comment text while preserving historical feed entry.

functions.signature: moderate_comment(comment_id: str, admin_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Allows administrators to remove non-compliant comment content.

business_rules: Uploaded files are untrusted and must never be used directly as filesystem paths.
File uploads must enforce size limits prior to unbounded data transfer.
Duplicate display names are permitted for different attachment uploads.
Attachments inherit the visibility and access rules of their parent work item or comment.
Downloading private files requires prior authentication and explicit authorization checks.
Temporary access URLs must have a strictly limited lifetime.

functions.signature: upload_attachment(parent_type: str, parent_id: str, user_id: str, filename: str, content: bytes) -> dict
functions.purpose: Uploads an attachment and associates it with a work item or comment.

functions.signature: generate_download_link(attachment_id: str, user_id: str) -> str
functions.purpose: Generates a secure temporary download link for an authorized user.

functions.signature: delete_attachment(attachment_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Removes an attachment from active view and normal access.

business_rules: Notifications trigger on relevant events like assignments, mentions, and followed item updates.
In-app notifications track read and unread status without requiring record deletion.
Email delivery failure must not roll back underlying database transactions or assignments.
Disabling email delivery does not automatically turn off in-app notifications.
Background notification processing must use idempotency mechanisms to avoid duplicate notifications on retry.

functions.signature: create_notification(user_id: str, event_type: str, resource_id: str, message: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Generates an in-app notification for a user.

functions.signature: mark_notification_as_read(notification_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Marks an in-app notification as read.

functions.signature: send_transactional_email(to_email: str, template_id: str, context: dict) -> bool
functions.purpose: Asynchronously dispatches a transactional email.

business_rules: Search indexes project names, descriptions, work item titles, descriptions, and comments.
Search operates strictly within the user's authorized organization and project boundaries.
Partial matching is supported over exact title queries.
Search indexing operates asynchronously and deleted items must be purged from results.
Search ranking is non-contractual and dynamic.

functions.signature: search_content(org_id: str, user_id: str, query: str, page: int = 1, page_size: int = 20) -> dict
functions.purpose: Executes a context-aware search across accessible operational content.

functions.signature: index_resource(resource_type: str, resource_id: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Submits a resource for asynchronous search indexing.

business_rules: The dashboard summarizes active projects and assigned work items for the current user.
Completed and archived work are omitted from default dashboard views.
Dashboard metrics are derived dynamically from accessible data rather than cached static facts.
Significant actions (creation, owner changes, assignments, status changes) produce immutable append-only activity records.
Activity records record actors and unambiguous timestamps, preserving actor identity even if user display names change or accounts deactivate.

functions.signature: get_user_dashboard(org_id: str, user_id: str) -> dict
functions.purpose: Retrieves summary metrics and active work assigned to the user.

functions.signature: get_activity_feed(org_id: str, user_id: str, project_id: str | None = None, page: int = 1, page_size: int = 20) -> dict
functions.purpose: Retrieves paginated historical activity records for an organization or project.

functions.signature: record_activity(org_id: str, event_type: str, actor_id: str | None, details: dict) -> dict
functions.purpose: Appends a new immutable event log entry to the activity history.
